name: Hot Snakes
label: Swami
lede: Hot Snakes made three records in five years in whatever weeks four calendars overlapped, with a singer in New York and a drummer in Philadelphia. A 2011 reunion brought a fourth album, and a fifth was very near done when Rick Froberg died in 2023.

eras.title: Pitchfork, then Drive Like Jehu
eras.text: John Reis and Rick Froberg made noise together in San Diego for more than a decade before Hot Snakes, first in Pitchfork, then in Drive Like Jehu.

years.src: Rolling Stone · Sub Pop: Hot Snakes
years.h: [[John Reis|626e7b64-3035-4f58-92a6-49790f600e30]] and [[Rick Froberg|07d99b38-fa92-4916-a190-1240b1d2e402]] start Pitchfork in San Diego
years.p: The quartet put out one album, Eucalyptus, in 1990. Sub Pop says the two had been collaborating since high school.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's obituary of Froberg dates Pitchfork to 1986 and calls it a San Diego quartet formed by Froberg and Reis. Sub Pop's Hot Snakes bio describes the pair as collaborators since high school, which makes Hot Snakes the third band in a partnership that had already run more than a decade.

years.h: Drive Like Jehu follow their debut with Yank Crime
years.p: Reis and Froberg's second band had put out a self-titled album in 1991. Rolling Stone describes the music as post-hardcore with complex time signatures.
years.xp: When Drive Like Jehu's reunion tours ran in 2015 and 2016, Reis told the Shepherd Express that they reignited his musical direction, and that the music of Hot Snakes was still current to what he was attracted to.

eras.title: A drummer in Philadelphia, a painter in New York
eras.text: Reis wanted to hear the sound in his head, and Rocket from the Crypt was between labels and short a drummer. Froberg's vocals turned the sessions into a band based in another city.

years.src: No Recess · Shepherd Express · Wikipedia: Hot Snakes
years.h: Reis and a Delta 72 drummer record 20 songs in two days
years.p: With [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]] between labels and without a drummer, Reis brings in Jason Kourkounis of [[The Delta 72|0e1a1b82-904f-49b0-8955-086f0bf28afa]], who lives in Philadelphia.
years.xp:
Reis told No Recess that Kourkounis flew out for a day or two, then came back for four days. They practiced for two of them, spent two days in the studio and recorded 20 songs. Reis has said he had the sound in his head and wanted to hear what it actually sounded like.

He tried the vocals himself first and decided against it. That is how the band ended up with a singer who lived in another city.

years.big: "He completely elevated all the songs, all the music; everything just got way better."
years.h: A singer in New York, a band in San Diego
years.p: Reis on Froberg, who had moved east to make art and joined from there.
years.xp: Froberg also drew all the band's artwork. Members were spread across San Diego, New York and Philadelphia. Wikipedia notes the geography is why touring and recording came in bursts.

years.h: Automatic Midnight comes out on Swami Records
years.p: Recorded in June 1999 at Big Fish Recorders in San Diego with engineer Ben Moore, it runs 31 minutes and 36 seconds.
years.xp: Froberg drew the artwork in black and white, but the packaging used translucent orange, so the finished record looked orange. Pitchfork gave it a 7.6 on release.

eras.title: Organ, a drummer swap, and the end
eras.text: Gar Wood is on bass, the band records in Reis's own practice space, and the sound gets stranger before it tightens. Mario Rubalcaba takes over the drums, a fall tour passes through John Peel's studio, and Reis calls it after Australia.

yt: Hot Snakes live at Michigan Fest, 2002
years.h: Suicide Invoice adds an organ and a melodica
years.p: Recorded at Reis's Drag Racist practice space, it puts a Magi 44 organ and a melodica into the songs. Pitchfork gave it an 8.8.
years.xp:
Reis told No Recess that he was inexperienced at recording there and that some logistics went wrong, and called it "a trial by jizz". He still thought the record turned out great. Drag Racist burned down the following year.

Frankie Stains plays organ on the closing song, "Paid in Cigarettes". Kourkounis is credited under the name Jsinclair.

years.h: [[Mario Rubalcaba|f1c57bba-a668-45fc-b35d-15fac1094cb4]] takes the sticks as Kourkounis joins Burning Brides
years.p: Rubalcaba had drummed for Rocket from the Crypt since 2000. Kourkounis left to play full time with Burning Brides.

years.src: Wikipedia: Audit in Progress · No Recess
years.h: Audit in Progress: Rubalcaba's first record with the band
years.p: Recorded at Big Fish Recorders and mastered by Dave Gardner, it won best punk album at the 2005 San Diego Music Awards.
years.xp: Reis called it "deconstructed rock 'n' roll" in the No Recess interview. Spin called it "loud, throttling punk-rock elegance". Its song "This Mystic Decade" later turned up on the Grand Theft Auto V soundtrack.

yt: Full show at the Casbah, San Diego, Nov 26, 2004
years.h: A Peel Session on the fall 2004 UK tour
years.p: Hot Snakes tape at John Peel's BBC studio, and the Peel Sessions EP follows in April 2005. Wikipedia calls it one of the last sessions for Peel's program, while Punknews headlined it his last ever.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Peel died shortly after the session. The sources differ on the wording, "one of the last" against "last ever", so both are attributed here.

The video is a full set from the same fall run, at the Casbah in San Diego on November 26, 2004.

years.h: Hot Snakes ends after an Australian tour
years.p: Reis stopped the band, and Rocket from the Crypt with it, to focus on being a father.
years.xp: Shepherd Express reports that Reis stopped both Hot Snakes and Rocket from the Crypt in 2005 to put fatherhood first. A live set from Australian radio, taped at the ABC's triple j studios in May 2005, came out the next year as Thunder Down Under.

eras.title: Obits, the Night Marchers, and one encore
eras.text: Reis kept Swami Records running and played in the Night Marchers with Wood and Kourkounis. Froberg started Obits. Then a three-song encore in San Diego in 2010 changed the mood.

years.h: The last thing they record is a Government Issue cover for Tony Hawk
years.p: Hot Snakes cut "Time to Escape" for the soundtrack of Tony Hawk's American Wasteland.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hot Snakes · No Recess · Shepherd Express
years.h: A May 2005 radio set from Australia comes out as Thunder Down Under
years.p: The band taped it at the ABC's triple j studios. The record came out on August 15, 2006, after the breakup.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it as a studio release, while No Recess and the Shepherd Express call it a live radio set.

years.h: Froberg's Obits and Reis's Night Marchers both start playing
years.p: Obits is Froberg's new band. Reis, Gar Wood and Kourkounis play together as the Night Marchers.

years.h: The original four play an unannounced encore at the Casbah
years.p: On July 29, 2010 in San Diego, the encore was "If Credit's What Matters I'll Take Credit", "Automatic Midnight" and "No Hands".
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the encore to July 29, 2010 at the Casbah and lists those three songs. The official reunion followed in 2011.

eras.title: Back, with a record this time
eras.text: The reunion began as festival dates and turned into a new album on Sub Pop, with all three old records reissued around it.

years.h: All Tomorrow's Parties and Fun Fun Fun Fest bring Hot Snakes back
years.p: West Coast dates follow in March and April 2012, then Metallica's Orion Music + More festival in New Jersey in June.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Kourkounis and Rubalcaba alternated on drums once the band was back.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hot Snakes · Sub Pop News: Hot Snakes reissues
years.h: Sub Pop announces a fall tour and a new album
years.p: In November Sub Pop scheduled reissues of all three Swami albums for January 2018, plus UK dates.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the first announcement to August 14, 2017: fall touring and a new record for Sub Pop.

years.cap: Hot Snakes at the Rock and Roll Hotel, Washington, DC
yt: Full performance, live on KEXP (Upstream Music Fest, 2018)
years.h: Fourteen years after Audit in Progress, Jericho Sirens
years.p: Ten songs in 30 minutes on Sub Pop. Froberg flew to California to write with Reis, and both Kourkounis and Rubalcaba drummed.
years.xp:
Exclaim! reports Kourkounis drummed on seven tracks and Rubalcaba on three. Froberg said of them: "They were both welcome to join in. We couldn't really say 'You can play and you can't.'"

Metacritic lists 86. Pitchfork gave it a 7.7.

years.h: "Not in Time" arrives with a hallucinatory video
years.p: Sub Pop released the video on a Thursday and pushed the song for Bandcamp Friday the next day.

eras.title: Rick
eras.text: The 2011 reunion ran until June 2023, with a fifth album close to done.

years.src: Rolling Stone · BrooklynVegan · Clash · mxdwn · Wikipedia: Hot Snakes
years.h: Rick Froberg dies at 55
years.p: John Reis announced it on Instagram: Froberg had died suddenly the night before, from natural causes. Two weeks earlier he had said a fifth Hot Snakes album was very near done.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone and Clash quote Reis writing: "Rick passed away suddenly last night from natural causes." BrooklynVegan reports that days later Froberg's girlfriend, Britt, wrote on his Instagram that the cause was an undiagnosed heart condition, which Wikipedia also states. Wikipedia gives the date as June 30, 2023.

Reis's statement also says: "The only thing he loved more than art and rock n roll was his friends."

In August 2023 Reis told an interviewer the band had been working on new music. He said it was every bit as good as, if not better than, the first Hot Snakes record.

years.h: Plenty For All collects Froberg's art
years.p: Akashic Books published a book of his pen and ink drawings, linocuts, paintings, watercolors and commercial work.
